Your own pages, Chat when you have a @reply, and nothing else: no built-in tabs, no pages from other apps on the machine, no other apps' chats.
The sidebar shows Chat and a My posts group with your two pages. Every layout of the app shell lists your pages in their group, and the layout picker still works.

You want Use The new app shell Nothing: style: app is the default. aiui.set_style("app") makes it explicit Only your pages aiui.only_my_pages() or aiui.set_pages([]) Your pages and Chat (minimal preset) aiui.set_pages("minimal") or aiui.only_my_pages("chat") (automatic default when running aiui run app.py with @aiui.page/@aiui.reply) Core Agent preset (Chat, Sessions, Approvals, Usage, Memory) aiui.set_pages("agent") or aiui run app.py --preset agent A few specific built-in pages aiui.set_pages(["chat", "sessions", "usage"]) (ids: aiui pages ids) Every page (full Ops console) aiui.set_pages("ops") / aiui.set_pages("all") or aiui run app.py --preset ops

Wrap any Python function (sync, async def, or streaming yield generator) into an interactive page without writing separate @aiui.page and @aiui.register_page_action handlers: set_pages is the one switch for what shows. It covers built-in pages, the app shell's layout pages (start, artifacts, templates, connect, api-reference) and dashboard-plugin folders, including the ones in ~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins that every app on the machine would otherwise share. Pages you register yourself (@aiui.page, aiui.register_page, aiui.register_plugin) always show. A wrong id is reported at startup: set_pages() names 'chta', but no page has that id.

A server-driven page: @aiui.page(id, title=..., icon=..., group=..., order=...) returning aiui.layout([...]) of blocks (aiui.metric, aiui.table, aiui.columns, aiui.markdown_text, aiui.card, ...). Pages with the same group sit together in the sidebar; order sorts them. Links: a page of markdown links, as links above. A React page or a whole plugin: see UI Plugins.

aiui run app.py keeps the app's chats in its own folder, ~/.praisonaiui/apps/ - /sessions/, so the sidebar never lists the chats of other apps or agents. Point it elsewhere with --datastore sdk:/path (or json:/path), or share the old machine-wide history with --datastore sdk. Set AIUI_DATA_DIR to move everything aiui keeps (config, sessions) for one app. See Sessions.

aiui.set_pages("all") (or aiui run app.py --pages all) is the opposite of a focused app: every page of the product, each in its React version where there is one and otherwise the legacy view inside the new shell, with every group (Agent, Work, Control, ...) listed in the sidebar of whatever layout is on. Your own pages still show in their group.

When you embed PraisonAIUI as a dedicated dashboard host and do not want agent/chat endpoints (/sessions, /run, /agents, /teams, /api/chat/*) mounted on the port, use aiui.create_shell_app() instead of create_app(). Pass csp="strict" (or a directive mapping / callable) to attach a strict Content-Security-Policy with the exact 'sha256-…' hashes of the shell's inline scripts — no HTML buffering middleware or manual route allowlists needed: GET /focus serves the plugin page under a strict script-src 'self' 'sha256-…' header; GET /sessions and other unmounted routes return 404. For custom hosts that render the HTML themselves, aiui.render_shell_html(request) returns (html, script_hashes) and aiui.shell_csp_header(html) formats the full header (connect-src 'self' covers same-origin WebSockets; pass extra= for any external host).
The list must hold only your page ids (and chat). Then open the page in a headless browser and look at the sidebar.

style: dashboard is the old vanilla UI. It still works (aiui run app.py --style dashboard, aiui.set_style("dashboard"), YAML style: dashboard or AIUI_SHELL=legacy, which prints a one-line notice), and set_pages applies there too, but new apps should not use it. Docs and examples that pass --style dashboard describe the legacy UI.
